dlg.brannoc.first.0.note: Each fragment set down like a weight. 'Good.' approving. The last fragment a statement of trade.

dlg.brannoc.first.1.note: Deep, slow, few words. 'Which?' a flat question.

dlg.brannoc.hub.1.note: Narrator: he keeps working and doesn't send you away. Then 'Steel or fur?' gentler than ever before.

dlg.brannoc.cloak.0.note: Pride; the last line a plain warning.

dlg.brannoc.irons.0.emo: cold suspicion, grief turned to anger
dlg.brannoc.irons.0.intent: he knows what the irons did
dlg.brannoc.irons.0.note: Narrator holds the long look. Then a ledger of facts, flat. A pause. The last line low and dangerous.

dlg.brannoc.irons.1.note: Facts, like reading a tally. 'Didn't ask who.' plain. Pause. 'Should've.' heavy, quiet regret.

dlg.brannoc.cb_wolf_slaughter.0.note: Three fragments. 'Wood'll be quiet.' a little too quiet.

dlg.brannoc.say_calling.2.note: Dismissive fragments; then 'Ferrule's loose. That is.' iron, his trade.

dlg.brannoc.say_calling.3.note: Four words, each tested like an edge.

dlg.brannoc.say_calling.4.note: Four words, each tested like an edge.

dlg.brannoc.t_brannoc.0.note: Fragments; a ghost of a smile on 'Worse temper.' 'Hammer's hers.' proud.

dlg.brannoc.mark.0.note: Narrator through the handling. 'Mine.' barely voiced. Narrator holds the long time. The second '...Mine.' broken.

dlg.brannoc.mark.1.note: 'Mine.' plain. Facts, flat. Narrator gives it back. 'It's done what it was for.' grim.

dlg.brannoc.irons_after.0.note: Low threat. 'Or herself.' a beat, he suspects. Narrator: the hammer comes down. 'I'll know the coin.' very quiet.

dlg.brannoc.nell.0.note: Narrator: he doesn't stop. Brannoc's facts come out like hammer strokes, too many words for him, which is the tell. 'Twelve. Red hair. New boots.' Narrator: the hammer stops. 'Mine. Nell.' Then the only question he ever asks, very quiet.

dlg.brannoc.nell_ditch.0.hides: he suspects whose coin paid for the irons
dlg.brannoc.nell_ditch.0.note: He does not break. Narrator gives the look at the irons. Then facts about his daughter, flat: 'Had the reins.' barely voiced. The love is only in saying 'the reins' again. No breath of his own: the narrator describes it.
dlg.brannoc.nell_ditch.0.beats: ...Had the reins. She'd want the reins. Always wanted the reins.

dlg.brannoc.nell_ditch.1.hides: he suspects whose coin paid for the irons
dlg.brannoc.nell_ditch.1.note: He does not break. Narrator: the hammer goes down, which you have never seen. 'Had the reins.' barely voiced. Narrator: the long breath (so none in his read). Flat facts about his daughter; the love is only in saying 'the reins' again.
dlg.brannoc.nell_ditch.1.beats: ...Had the reins. | She'd want the reins. Always wanted the reins.

dlg.brannoc.nell_gone.0.note: 'Quick, then. Water's quick.' a man holding himself up. Narrator for the hammer. 'Forge is shut. Go on.' near breaking, then steady.

dlg.brannoc.nell_risen.0.intent: she rose and you killed her
dlg.brannoc.nell_risen.0.note: Narrator: he looks at you. 'Got up.' weighed. Narrator explains how he says it. Then slowly, all of it. A long pause. 'Was it quick?' the most fragile thing he says.

dlg.brannoc.nell_quick.0.note: The only thanks he gives in the game. Narrator holds the long time. '...Thank you.' barely there, deep and cracked. Narrator: the forge cools. 'Forge is shut. Go on.' quiet.

dlg.brannoc.nell_slow.0.note: Narrator: he nods as if told a price. 'Forge is shut.' flat, final.

dlg.brannoc.nell_lie.0.note: Narrator for each hammer stroke. 'Low Kiln, then. Good.' relief. 'Aunt'll feed her up. She's thin.' tender, which makes the lie worse.

dlg.brannoc.nell_look.0.note: Repeats it flat. Narrator for the hammer. 'No.' Then quiet bitterness: 'Nobody looks.'
